local_facts.title: A crash report can still leave a separate 10-day DMV task
local_facts.claim: California DMV requires an SR-1 within 10 days when a crash causes any injury or death, or more than $1,000 in property damage; it is separate from a police, CHP, or insurance report.
local_facts.why_it_matters: A Modesto collision file can have a CHP or police report and still carry an independent DMV reporting deadline.

local_facts.title: The familiar 15/30/5 shorthand is not the current floor
local_facts.claim: California raised standard auto-policy minimum liability limits as policies renewed beginning January 1, 2025, from $15,000/$30,000/$5,000 to $30,000/$60,000/$15,000.
local_facts.why_it_matters: The crash and policy-renewal dates affect which limits are relevant, and a minimum limit is not a measure of the full loss.

local_facts.title: Stanislaus County’s traffic-injury volume makes early evidence practical
local_facts.claim: The California Office of Traffic Safety recorded 4,679 people killed or injured in Stanislaus County traffic collisions in 2023, including 389 fatal-and-injury hit-and-run collisions.
local_facts.why_it_matters: In a county with this volume of serious crash events, report requests, camera preservation, witness details, and insurance records need early attention.
